exercise.name: Copenhagen Plank
steps: Lie on your side next to a bench, propped up on your forearm.
Place your top foot or knee on the bench.
Lift your hips until your body is straight, lower leg off the floor.
Hold, then lower and switch sides.
exercise.one_line_summary: A hold (one picture): side plank on the right forearm (elbow under the shoulder), top (left) leg straight with the ankle resting on a flat bench, bottom (right) leg straight and lifted just under the bench, hips up so head-shoulders-hips-ankles make one line. The top leg's adductors hold the body up; obliques and abs hold the trunk.

setup.target: Bottom forearm on the floor, elbow straight under the shoulder, forearm pointing forward.
setup.tolerance: elbow within 0.05 m of under the shoulder
setup.why: Side-plank base; S4 'support yourself on your forearm'.

setup.target: Long lever: top leg straight, inside of the ankle/foot on a flat bench (seat top 0.44 m).
setup.tolerance: knee 0-10 deg; ankle on the pad 0.05-0.10 m in from its edge
setup.why: S2: the long lever gives higher peak and mean adductor torque than the short (knee) lever; S4: ankle on bench = longest lever. Library allows foot or knee; the foot version is the one the name usually shows.

setup.target: Straight, lifted off the floor, under the bench (pressing up toward it).
setup.tolerance: foot clear of the floor; does not touch the bench frame
setup.why: Library step 3 (lower leg off the floor); S4 'press it up into the underside of the bench'.

setup.target: Hips up, no sag, no forward rotation of hips or shoulders.
setup.tolerance: hip within 0.04 m of the shoulder-ankle line
setup.why: S4 common mistakes: sagging hips, rotating forward.

movement.measure: body line tilt along its length; root rot (0, -86, -90) = on the right side, head +Y, chest -X
top leg in line with the trunk, ankle on the bench
movement.path: Held: the adductors pull the body up toward the top leg.

muscles.emg: Copenhagen adduction is one of the two high-intensity adductor exercises; adductor longus peak nEMG across the 8 exercises 14-108% MVC (S1, abstract gives the range only). Long lever > short lever for peak and mean torque (S2). Modified vs standard stage-1 position: no difference in adductor longus EMG (S3).
muscles.role: Pull the body up toward the supported top leg; what the exercise is for.
muscles.surface: Inner thigh, from the pubic bone down the inside of the thigh toward the knee.

muscles.emg: Abdominal peak nEMG 5-48% MVC across the adduction exercises (S1); side planks give high oblique EMG in general (S4 lists obliques).
muscles.role: Hold the trunk up sideways (anti side-bend).
Keeps the trunk from twisting or arching.
Hold the hips level and extended.
muscles.surface: Buttock and side of the hip.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: The pelvis drops below the shoulder-ankle line.
mistakes.why_it_matters: S4: usually obliques not engaged; less adductor load.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Hips and shoulders turn toward the floor.

sources.citation: Serner A, Jakobsen MD, Andersen LL, Holmich P, Sundstrup E, Thorborg K. 2014. EMG evaluation of hip adduction exercises for soccer players: implications for exercise selection in prevention and treatment of groin injuries. Br J Sports Med 48(14):1108-1114. doi:10.1136/bjsports-2012-091746
sources.what_it_gave: Copenhagen adduction = high-intensity adductor exercise; adductor longus 14-108% MVC across exercises; gluteal and abdominal 5-48%.

sources.citation: Marusic J, Cvjeticanin O, Supej M, Babic J, Sarabon N. 2026. Biomechanics of Copenhagen adduction exercise and eccentric hip adductor exercises on a novel isokinetic dynamometer with within-session repeatability. Scand J Med Sci Sports 36(9):e70365. doi:10.1111/sms.70365
sources.what_it_gave: Long-lever Copenhagen gives higher peak and mean adductor torque than short lever.

sources.citation: Hinnekens S, Fickers E, Vervloet G. 2024. Effectiveness of the Copenhagen adduction modified position stage 1: EMG measurements and hand-held dynamometer analysis in young and healthy men. J Bodyw Mov Ther 39:251-257. doi:10.1016/j.jbmt.2024.02.017
sources.what_it_gave: Adductor longus EMG and force similar in modified and standard positions.
Forearm on the floor; top leg knee (short), calf (mid) or ankle (long) on the bench; bottom leg straight under the bench; straight line; mistakes: sagging, rotating forward, breath holding.

clip_check.check: Support elbow under the shoulder, forearm on the floor
clip_check.target: elbow within 0.05 m of under the right shoulder; forearm z 0.02-0.05

clip_check.check: Top ankle rests on the bench pad
clip_check.target: gap -0.01..+0.01 m to the pad top (0.44)

clip_check.check: Bottom leg off the floor, not through the bench
clip_check.target: lowest leg point > 0.1 m; no overlap with seat, post or rail
hip within 0.04 m of the shoulder-ankle line
inner thigh (adductors) strongest red; obliques and abs light
